title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - trivia

This system parallels the prophecy of the Chosen Undead and their becoming a Lord of Cinder.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Gwyn's act of linking the First Flame came to be a point of controversy for several figures; namely Kaathe and Aldia would regard Gwyn's sacrifice as having "unnaturally" extended an Age of Fire that was never meant to last, inhibiting the potential of humans in the process. As of the time of the Chosen Undead, one consequence of Kaathe's actions lies beneath Firelink Shrine: the ruins of New Londo, which was captured by the Darkstalker and had to be flooded before the Abyss within could spread to the surface world.

title: Lothric
snippet: When the royal family realized that Lothric would not improve from his condition, they resorted to repulsive acts in an attempt to obtain a worthy Champion for the linking: the rulers bound the souls of the two princes together with a curse. Although the exact motive behind this act is unknown, it is likely that the rulers intended for Prince Lothric to draw out some of the strength of his elder brother's soul, which could have allowed him to qualify as worthy Ash for the First Flame. It was even said that Lorian willingly submitted to the curse, even as it crippled him. The resulting Soul of the Twin Princes was one worthy of providing kindling for the First Flame, even as the princes were physically incapable of overcoming the obstacles involved in linking the Flame. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chamber to await the end of the world.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In Ending 2: "The End of Fire", the First Flame is snuffed out, albeit with the Fire Keeper revealing that one day "tiny flames will dance across the darkness", which suggests that the First Flame partially perseveres in the form of embers within the Lords of Cinder of the past. As these Lords will use these embers of the First Flame to exert influence the world, this Age of Dark does not spell finality for the Flame. Alternatively, the player can choose to intervene as the Fire Keeper is about to extinguish the First Flame, by killing her before the cinematic ends. In this ending, the Ashen One instead takes the First Flame for themselves while the final segment of the opening narration is heard: *"Nameless, accursed Undead, unfit even to be cinder...And so it is...that Ash seeketh embers."*

title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
Chosen Undead -  Dark Souls - character - epilogue

It is here that the Chosen Undead may make their decision of either linking the flame or walking away from it. ***Link the Fire:** This ending is unlocked if the player rekindles the First Flame. The Chosen Undead offers themselves as kindling to the fire. Sacrificing all of their souls, the Chosen Undead is consumed by the flames and the Age of Fire is extended, as life is breathed into the First Flame once more.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Studying and experimenting on the inhuman creatures and their souls, and via studies on artifacts from older kingdoms, Vendrick and Aldia pioneered the creation of Golems, very similar in appearance to the captured giants. Vendrick made Nashandra his queen, and had the golems build his Royal Castle, as proof of his gratitude and affection to her. Beneath the royal castle was the ancient Throne of Want, an artifact capable of connecting to the First Flame, the source of souls and beginning of all that the king was seeking. Studying the First Flame and the mysteries of the soul with his brother Aldia, the king acquired a profound understanding of the history of the world and the rules of reality, how the Flame brought Disparity and everything from it, propagating souls in the world every time someone linked it, giving it new strength. He also understood how the Dark was kept under control as long as the fire flourished, and that once the fire naturally weakened the curse would strike

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: The deformed Aldia is encountered several times by the Bearer of the Curse, to whom he imparts his extensive knowledge on the nature of life. He expresses outrage over the actions of the Lord of Light, who cursed humans into mortality and introduced the cycle of light and dark by linking the First Flame. Aldia's bleak worldview considers mankind as "props on the stage of life", persevering merely through obsession. While acknowledging the merits of the Age of Fire, he labels the roots of this "warm, resplendent" world as a lie, with the linking of the Fire as its original sin. Nevertheless, Aldia realizes that one could wish to inherit this order, even if built on a "tender, exquisite" lie. Instead of submission to the peace provided by the status quo, he offers a third "path"; obscure and unpaved, yet could perhaps ascend the scope of Light and Dark.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Now bereft of most of his Lord Soul's power and with only the power of his soul, Gwyn left for the Kiln of the First Flame, the structure built to house and protect it, with only his robes, his mighty greatsword and his powerless crown, accompanied only by a guard of Black Knights. Eventually Gwyn linked the First Flame, prolonging its life but himself being consumed by it, reduced to the empty husk of cinders guarding the core of the Kiln. The inferno of the newly kindled fire melted the surroundings and burned his knights to ashes, leaving them to wander the world as disembodied spirits.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Dark Lord
snippet:
Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

At the end of the game, after defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One, in case they chose to link the First Flame, is covered from head to toe in a soft-looking fire, unlike the flaming inferno of the first game. The implications are clear: The First Flame itself now is so weak that it cannot be kindled anymore.

The First Flame, as the Age of Fire, is beyond saving.

snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - soul_of_cinder 
 soul_of_cinder : After returning to the shrine, the Ashen One places the ashes of the Lords on their thrones, and the Firekeeper channels their strength to the Ashen One. The Firekeeper bids the Ashen One travel to the First Flame. Accepting the strength of the Lords, the Ashen One is transported to a copy of the Firelink shrine, standing amid the wreckage of kingdoms. From there, the Ashen One proceeds to the Kiln of the First Flame.

There they encounter the Soul of Cinder, a manifestation of the Lords that had previously linked the flame. The Soul of Cinder takes on many forms and fighting styles, mimicking those who had linked the flame. Once the Ashen One weakens it, the Soul of Cinder assumes the style of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, first one to link the flame. After defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One is presented with four options depending on the choices they made.

title: Ashen One

 road_of_sacrifices_and_crucifixion_woods : Following the road leads the Ashen One to the Crucifixion Woods, where they encounter Anri of Astora and their companion Horace the Hushed. Anri seeks Aldrich, and thinks to find him in the Cathedral of the Deep. They offer their help to the Ashen One, should the Ashen One need it. Here the Ashen One may also find Orbeck of Vinheim, a sorcerer who will offer to share his knowledge if the Ashen One brings him magic scrolls.

Making their way through the Crucifixion Woods leads the Ashen One to a crossroads. One path leads to Farron Keep, home of the Abyss Watchers, whereas the other one, guarded by one of the Crystal Sages, leads to the Cathedral of the Deep, home of Aldrich.

title: Ashen One

 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

Upon encountering the Ashen One, Yoel offers his services, providing rudimentary sorceries and offering to draw out the Ashen One's "true strength", not telling them that doing so will burden the Ashen One with the Dark Sigil which will make them hollow upon death.

Inside the Settlement, the Ashen One is accosted by the inhabitants of the town and pelted with massive arrows by a Giant atop a tower. After fighting and killing the Curse-rotted Greatwood, the Ashen One will find a Transposing Kiln that will allow Ludleth to provide great spells and weapons from the souls of powerful creatures.

 grand_archives_and_prince_lothric : Progressing through Lothric Castle will bring the Ashen One face to face with a Dragonslayer Armour controlled by a Pilgrim Butterfly. Defeating the armour opens the way to the Grand Archives, home to ancient knowledge.

The Ashen One fights their way through the Archives, and find themselves close to the location of Prince Lothric, who hides at the very top of the castle. Lothric has no intention of returning as a Lord of Cinder however, preferring to watch the world end from afar with his brother Lorian. The brothers attack the Ashen One, who slays them both, and claims Lothric's ashes.

A knight in the cover is named as 'Red Knight' in the Funko Pop! line.
**There’s a misconception about the Soul of Cinder armor and the Red Knight armor: They are essentially the same Firelink set, the only difference being that the Red Knight (Ashen One) version has a tabard, while the Soul of Cinder version does not.
**The Red Knight armor is a variant of the Firelink set, distinguished by its tabard bearing a coat of arms reminiscent of the Lothric Knights.
In the Pre-Alpha *Dark Souls III*, the Ashen One is shown to use a cut-content weapon called the Legion Scimitars. Its dual combat art Spin Slash was ultimately given to the Sellsword Twinblades, while its design was relegated to a curved sword named Scimitar.

Fighting their way past the gargoyles and priestesses that guard the way to the giant, the Ashen One finds him atop his throne. The enormously strong and durable Yhorm initially seems insurmountable, but the Ashen One finds the magic blade Storm Ruler, a sword with the ability to fell giants, beside his throne. title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

There are four **endings to *Dark Souls III***.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet:
Fire Keeper -  Dark Souls III - character - general_information 
 general_information : In *Dark Souls*, bonfires watched over by Fire Keepers are automatically kindled to provide ten Estus Flask charges each. Still they may be upgraded through the Rite of Kindling, just like other bonfires. All Fire Keepers have special souls and drop a Fire Keeper Soul upon death. Fire Keepers universally share the ability to upgrade Estus Flasks using the souls of their fellow Fire Keepers. The death or departure of a Fire Keeper will lead to the bonfire they attended to be extinguished, and it can no longer be used to rest, level up or teleport from using the Lordvessel. The description of the regular Fire Keeper Soul states that "Each Fire Keeper is a corporeal manifestation of her bonfire, and a draw for the humanity which is offered to her."

title: Fire Keeper
snippet:
In *Dark Souls II*, the three Fire Keepers in Things Betwixt and the Emerald Herald, believed by some to be Fire Keeper, can be killed without the nearby bonfire being affected. The way the Herald can level up the Bearer of the Curse is reminescent of how the Fire Keepers in *Dark Souls III* can the Ashen One. One of the Keepers, Strowen, offers the player to re-allocate their attributes in exchange for a Soul Vessel.

In *Dark Souls III*, the unnamed Fire Keeper can level up the Ashen One like the Hemerald did in the previous game. She is also immortal; killing her, in addition to not causing the Shrine bonfire to be affected, will only cause her to respawn upon reloading the area, claiming that she cannot die. Instead of a Keeper, it is Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth, the leader of the Rosaria's Fingers covenant, who allows the player to re-allocate their attributes.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet: All Fire Keepers in the series suffer substantial ailments: Anastacia has neither tongue nor feet, Quelaag's Sister is gravely ill in addition to being twisted by the Flame of Chaos, and the Darkmoon Knightess has a "ghastly form" and "hideous swarms of humanity" hidden under her armor, while the unnamed *Dark Souls III* Fire Keeper, seemingly all of her Lothric predecessors, the Old Ladies, and Irina are all blind. The Emerald Herald, who might be a Keeper, has no visible affliction, although she claims that she "did not come out as intended".

title: Fire Keeper
snippet: All confirmed Fire Keepers in the series, as well as prospective Fire Keeper Irina of Carim and the possible Fire Keepers that are the Emerald Herald and mentionned fourth sister in *Dark Souls II*, are female, as are seemingly all of the dead Fire Keepers whose bodies can be found in the Firelink Shrine of *Dark Souls III*. The description of the generic Fire Keeper Soul in *Dark Souls* similarly refers to "Each Fire Keeper" using female pronouns. Whether the reason is cultural or biological is unclear.

title: Lothric
snippet:
The relations between the two realms soon blossomed into an alliance, formalized by the incorporation of the sword of Lothric, a symbol of that realm, into the insignia of the Blades of the Darkmoon, the predecessors of the Blue Sentinels and the Way of Blue. In practice, the unification of cultural and religious symbols of the kingdoms allowed the usage of transport demons by those bearing the banner of Lothric.

Now in possession of the knowledge provided by the primordial serpents and the ancient gods of Anor Londo, the kingdom of Lothric developed its role in the linking of the Flame, building the Firelink Shrine just outside the city walls, neighbouring the Royal Gardens, in order to guarantee safe and regulated passage to the Kiln of the First Flame. The shrine would once again accept Fire Keepers who assisted Champions that aspired to link the Flame, drawing out the strength of the souls they acquired to aid them in their journey.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Yhorm refused to serve as fuel for the First Flame a second time due to the fact that, once awakened from his grave, he realized that his sacrifice had been futile. The sorcerers of the Profaned Capital had continued to experiment on the Profaned Flame he had tried to quell with his sacrifice and as a result the entire city was destroyed, making his life of service meaningless even after the end. The moment he rises from the grave, he can be seen already howling in despair. In addition, he may also have simply understood the state of the world, now corrupted beyond any possibility of traditional salvation through the linking of the Fire, and simply decided to await death in the ruins of his city.
